reveals.label: Cell 1: Vector + Mechanism
reveals.question: 1. What viral vector and silencing mechanism does uniQure's AMT-130 gene therapy use?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Recombinant AAV5 delivering an artificial microRNA (miHTT) that degrades HTT mRNA via RNA interference (RNAi)
reveals.answer: Recombinant AAV5 delivering an artificial microRNA (miHTT) that degrades HTT mRNA via RNA interference (RNAi)

reveals.label: Cell 2: Surgical route
reveals.question: 2. How is AMT-130 physically delivered across the Blood-Brain Barrier into the striatum?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Single neurosurgical MRI-guided Convection-Enhanced Delivery (CED) infusion into the caudate and putamen
reveals.answer: Single neurosurgical MRI-guided Convection-Enhanced Delivery (CED) infusion into the caudate and putamen

reveals.label: Cell 3: Distinction critique
reveals.question: 3. State two major limitations of the AMT-130 Phase I/II clinical trial data (NCT04120493).
reveals.expectedAnswer: Small cohort size, sham control unblinding after 12m, irreversible surgery, and non-selective knockdown of wild-type HTT
reveals.answer: Small cohort size, sham control unblinding after 12m, irreversible surgery, and non-selective knockdown of wild-type HTT

reveals.label: Cell 4: Allele-selective
reveals.question: 4. How do synthetic Zinc Finger Proteins (ZFPs) improve selectivity compared to non-allele-specific RNAi?
reveals.expectedAnswer: ZFPs bind specifically to expanded CAG repeats at the DNA level to repress mutant HTT transcription while sparing normal wild-type HTT
reveals.answer: ZFPs bind specifically to expanded CAG repeats at the DNA level to repress mutant HTT transcription while sparing normal wild-type HTT

reveals.label: Cell 5: Exact count = 3
reveals.question: 5. How many management options must learners assess to satisfy Distinction criterion D5?
reveals.expectedAnswer: EXACTLY THREE available options covering patient care, well-being, treatments, or family outcomes
reveals.answer: EXACTLY THREE available options covering patient care, well-being, treatments, or family outcomes

reveals.label: Cell 6: Holistic MDT
reveals.question: 6. Name three allied health professionals in a Huntington's Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) and their roles.
reveals.expectedAnswer: Physiotherapist (gait/falls), Occupational Therapist (adaptive aids), Speech & Language Therapist (dysphagia/swallowing), Dietitian (high-calorie nutrition)
reveals.answer: Physiotherapist (gait/falls), Occupational Therapist (adaptive aids), Speech & Language Therapist (dysphagia/swallowing), Dietitian (high-calorie nutrition)

objectives.knowledge: Synthesise current clinical evidence on emerging Huntington's gene therapies (AMT-130 AAV5-miHTT, CRISPR-Cas9, synthetic ZFPs, siRNA/ASOs) from primary research sources (D3).
objectives.application: Discuss the clinical, surgical, regulatory, and timeline relevance of gene therapies for symptomatic Ben versus his asymptomatic young/unborn children in the case study context (D3).
objectives.evaluation: Critically assess exactly three available management options for Huntington's disease outcomes in Ben's family context (weighing efficacy, risks, accessibility, ethics, and quality of life) and audit all 11 Task 2 criteria (D5).

terminology.def: Investigational AAV5 gene therapy delivered by stereotactic MRI-guided CED into the striatum; Phase I/II (NCT04120493) showed CSF mHTT/NfL lowering and up to 75% cUHDRS slowing at 36 months, but remains experimental (small N, irreversible surgery).
Distinction concept: gene-silencing therapies like AMT-130 aim to slow further striatal neurodegeneration rather than regenerate already lost medium spiny neurons.
Engineered DNA-binding repressors designed to target expanded CAG repeats selectively at the DNA transcription stage, sparing the normal wild-type HTT allele.
Pharmacological agents that deplete presynaptic dopamine in striatal synapses to reduce involuntary motor chorea, requiring monitoring for depression and sedation side effects.
Integrated NHS specialist care combining neurology, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech & language therapy (dysphagia), dietetics, neuropsychology, and HDA family advocacy.

theoryPoints: D3 — Synoptic Relevance of Gene Therapies in Ben's Case Study Context (PO3): Critically evaluate 4 modalities from notebook sources: (1) AMT-130 (AAV5-miHTT via CED — strongest human clinical signal: dose-dependent CSF mHTT/NfL drop & up to 75% cUHDRS deceleration at 36m in Phase I/II NCT04120493, BUT small cohort, sham unblinding after 12m, non-allele-specific knockdown of wild-type HTT, invasive irreversible brain surgery, not yet NHS-licensed/NICE-approved); (2) CRISPR-Cas9 (permanent DNA editing/NHEJ knockout, but off-target DSBs, delivery across BBB, somatic-only under UK HFEA law); (3) Synthetic ZFPs (allele-selective transcriptional repression in R6/2 mice — still preclinical); (4) siRNA/ASOs (repeatable intrathecal delivery, e.g. Alnylam/tominersen lessons, transient effect requiring repeated lumbar punctures).

D3 Nuanced Clinical Verdict (Ben vs Children): For 40-year-old SYMPTOMATIC Ben right now, gene therapies are NOT currently an available NHS cure (cannot reverse existing striatal loss; trial eligibility is highly restrictive) — though clinical trial monitoring may offer future disease-slowing hope. Conversely, for Ben's 6yo, 3yo, and unborn children (if any inherit H, symptoms likely 25–40 years away), mature licensed gene therapies (AMT-130/ZFP/CRISPR) are far more realistically relevant as future presymptomatic disease-modifying interventions!

D5 — Assessing EXACTLY THREE Available Management Options in the Case Study Context (PO3): Must provide balanced clinical appraisal (strengths, limitations, risks, cost/access, patient & family impact) of THREE concrete available options: (1) Pharmacological Symptom Control (VMAT2 inhibitors like tetrabenazine/deutetrabenazine for chorea, SSRIs for depression/anxiety — improves daily function & dignity at work/home, but non-curative and tetrabenazine can worsen depression/suicidality!); (2) Multidisciplinary Supportive & Rehabilitative Care (Physiotherapy for gait/falls, OT for adaptive tools/workplace adjustments, SLT for dysphagia/aspiration prevention, high-calorie dietetics for chorea weight loss, neuropsychology + HDA — holistic QoL and carer support for wife/children, zero surgical risk, but labour-intensive and cannot halt neuronal death); (3) Reproductive & Familial Risk Management (NHS genetic counselling + prenatal CVS/amniocentesis for current pregnancy and/or IVF with PGD/PGT-M for future family planning — breaks generational transmission cycle, but carries miscarriage risk, termination trauma, IVF physical/financial burden, and does not treat Ben's own progression).

Final 11-Criterion Quality Audit (P8–P12, M5–M7, D3–D5): Verify every criterion hits the exact OCR command verb ('Summarise', 'Explain', 'Create', 'Analyse', 'Discuss', 'Assess'), honours the 'Patient' vs 'Case Study Context' boundary, and cites primary sources in flawless Harvard format.

workedExample.title: Writing Distinction-Grade 'Discuss' (D3) and 'Assess' (D5) Evaluations
workedExample.subtitle: Moving from Merit description to balanced, evidence-weighted clinical judgement

steps.label: Step 1 — D3 Balanced Clinical Discussion (Gene Therapies)
steps.detail: Weigh exciting Phase I/II AMT-130 data (up to 75% cUHDRS slowing, CSF mHTT & NfL reduction) directly against structural limitations (small N, sham unblinding, non-selective wild-type HTT lowering, irreversible neurosurgery, unlicensed on NHS). Conclude by contrasting limited immediate relevance for symptomatic Ben against high future relevance for any mutation-positive child in 20+ years.

steps.label: Step 2 — D5 Three-Option Structured Assessment
steps.detail: Assess Option 1 (Pharmacological: tetrabenazine + SSRIs), Option 2 (MDT Rehabilitative/Psychosocial: Physio, OT, SLT, Dietetics, Psychology, HDA), and Option 3 (Reproductive/Familial: Counselling, Prenatal Testing, IVF-PGD) using identical criteria: clinical benefit, side effects/risks, NHS availability, and impact on Ben + wife + children.

steps.label: Step 3 — Integrated Clinical Recommendation (Distinction Capstone)
steps.detail: Synthesise a justified holistic care plan: combine immediate Option 1 (carefully titrated chorea/mood medication) + Option 2 (early MDT & HDA family support) for Ben's quality of life now, alongside Option 3 (non-directive reproductive counselling) for family planning — while keeping Ben registered with UK HD research registries for future gene-therapy trials.

hingeQuestions.question: Why is it critical for Distinction D3 to distinguish between Ben's immediate clinical timeline and his children's long-term timeline when discussing gene therapies like AMT-130?
options: Because AMT-130 is already sold over-the-counter in UK pharmacies for adults

Because AMT-130/CRISPR/ZFPs remain experimental and cannot reverse already-lost neurons in symptomatic 40-year-old Ben today, whereas if a young child inherits H, licensed disease-modifying gene therapies may realistically be available decades before adult onset
Because children under 10 are routinely given germline CRISPR editing on the NHS
Because gene therapy only works in people who are adopted
hingeQuestions.explanation: Distinction D3 demands case-study context evaluation: realistic short-term limitations for symptomatic Ben (unlicensed, irreversible surgery, non-regenerative) juxtaposed with transformative medium-to-long-term potential for his at-risk children.

hingeQuestions.question: Which critical clinical trade-off MUST be noted when assessing tetrabenazine (a VMAT2 inhibitor) as a pharmacological management option for Ben under D5?
options: It permanently edits the HTT gene in striatal neurons

While effective at suppressing involuntary motor chorea via dopamine depletion, it carries a major risk of worsening clinical depression and suicidal ideation — a particular danger given Ben's P9 mental health vulnerability
It is completely free of side effects and cures cognitive decline
It prevents Huntington's disease from being passed to unborn children
hingeQuestions.explanation: Linking tetrabenazine's depression/suicidality side-effect profile directly back to Ben's mental health risk (P9) is a hallmark of high-scoring synoptic Distinction evaluation in D5.

plenary: D3 mastery: Weigh promising AMT-130/CRISPR/ZFP/RNAi evidence against surgical, biological, and regulatory realities — contrasting symptomatic Ben today versus his children's future horizon.

D5 mastery: Deliver a balanced, evidence-based assessment of THREE available options (Pharmacological, MDT Supportive Care, Reproductive/PGD) culminating in an integrated recommendation for Ben's family.
Final NEA Task 2 Audit: Every criterion from P8–P12, M5–M7, and D3–D5 verified against OCR command verbs, scope boundaries, and Harvard citations!
